item.title: iOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3 add Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode, and more to Safari (3 minute read)
item.description: Apple is introducing vertical tabs in Safari's developer betas across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with tabs displayed as compact icons in a left sidebar that can expand to show website titles. A new Adaptive Dark Mode can automatically generate dark versions of websites that lack native support, either on demand or through a persistent preference. Siri AI can also organize, sort, move, and close tabs, with broader awareness of webpage content planned for a future update.

item.title: Adobe Premiere Mobile App is Getting Licensed Music from Universal and Warner Music (2 minute read)
item.description: Adobe is bringing licensed tracks from Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group into its Premiere mobile app, searchable by genre and duration. Videos using them can be shared on social media without copyright strikes, though only for personal use. Each video can include no more than 60 seconds of a song.

item.title: Canva to Cut More Than 1000 Jobs in ‘Hardest Moment' of Its History (4 minute read)
item.description: Canva is restructuring 1,271 roles, affecting 22 percent of its workforce, after its growth slowed this year for the first time in a decade. Chief executive Melanie Perkins called it the hardest moment in Canva's thirteen-year history, announcing a merged product organization with fewer management layers. Departing staff receive at least six months' salary, and the cuts follow Canva slashing its own valuation to US$31 billion.

item.title: Agents struggle with the same bad UX we do (7 minute read)
item.description: Computer-use AI agents frequently fail at the same confusing interfaces that frustrate humans, including ambiguous buttons, hidden menus, unexplained disabled states, and disruptive overlays. People often compensate for these problems by guessing, backtracking, or relying on experience, while agents expose the underlying design debt through repeatable failures that are easier to observe. Making interfaces clearer for agents through explicit labels, visible states, predictable interactions, and semantic structure can also improve accessibility and usability for people.

item.title: Everyone is building AI agents. Who's designing the stop button? (17 minute read)
item.description: AI agents introduce unpredictable behavior into products traditionally designed around explicit rules and known transitions, making it essential to distinguish where autonomy is useful from where reliability is mandatory. Products can let AI interpret intentions and construct workflows while using deterministic execution, visible uncertainty, confirmation steps, and clear recovery mechanisms to protect consequential actions. Designing effective agent experiences increasingly means defining boundaries around what AI may decide, when humans must intervene, and how users can understand, correct, or stop an autonomous process.

item.title: Why 10,000 experiments work better than 10,000 hours for designers (6 minute read)
item.description: Repeatedly practicing the same design skills can make someone better at their current job without developing the problem-framing, influence, and decision-making abilities required for more senior roles. Instead of relying on experience alone, designers can break career goals into microskills and run small experiments, such as opening every design review with a specific decision or presenting research findings themselves. A weekly reflection can help turn these experiments into deliberate professional growth without requiring organizational approval or major changes to existing workflows.

item.title: Bad AI Doesn't Smell (4 minute read)
item.description: Like a bad survey, bad AI output gives no sign that it's wrong, but authority bias, truth bias, and algorithm appreciation make people trust it anyway. In user research, mistranscriptions, missed body language, misread sarcasm, and hallucinations can turn into confident, wrong insights. Someone who ran the research has to check any AI analysis, ideally used only as a sense-check after doing their own.

item.title: Tokenizer Mono (30 minute read)
item.description: Tokenizer Mono is an experimental typeface based on IBM Plex Mono that visualizes how language models split text into tokens, using OpenType features to highlight boundaries directly as someone types without running a tokenizer in JavaScript. Its 28 styles represent different tokenizers from OpenAI, Meta, Google, DeepSeek, and others, combining contextual glyph substitutions with built-in color palettes to approximate token boundaries. Most styles achieve roughly 98% agreement with real tokenizers in testing, demonstrating how advanced font technology can perform surprisingly complex text processing while revealing its limitations around line breaks, uncommon words, and tokenization algorithms.

item.title: How Afternow put Kinetik's identity and four products into one system (5 minute read)
item.description: Afternow redesigned healthcare transportation platform Kinetik around painterly city landscapes inspired by the view from a car window, replacing conventional clinical imagery with a warmer visual language built from purple, deep greens, gold, salmon, and lavender. GT Alpina provides expressive editorial typography, DM Sans supports accessible product interfaces, and AI-generated landscapes are carefully art-directed with documented prompts to maintain consistency. The identity extends across four products through a shared design system containing more than 300 components and 2,000 screens, using tokens to adapt spacing, density, and accessibility for administrators, transportation providers, and elderly patients.

item.title: Dutch Digital Artist Creates the Most Warm, Ethereal Artworks You Will Ever Lay Eyes On (1 minute read)
item.description: Utrecht-based digital artist and animator Lois van Baarle, known as Loish, paints expressive female figures in soft, glowing light, rich color, and flowing hair and clothing.

item.title: Chrome's new menu search makes settings and bookmarks easier to find (2 minute read)
item.description: Google is testing a searchable three-dot menu in Chrome that lets users find browser commands, bookmarks, and recently visited websites without navigating through nested menus.

item.title: Designing Product Demos People Can Actually Follow (7 minute read)
item.description: A product demo is a sequence of state changes, so clarity depends on how attention moves between steps rather than on polished screens.

item.title: iPhone 18 will have two upgrades inspired by ‘Pro' models, per leak (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple's upcoming iPhone 18 will reportedly inherit two improvements from the iPhone 18 Pro: longer battery life and a more efficient processor. The new A20 chip is expected to use TSMC's 2-nanometer manufacturing process, potentially delivering significant performance and efficiency gains over previous generations. The standard model is expected in early 2027, but the smaller Dynamic Island will reportedly remain exclusive to Pro models, and a price increase is possible.

item.title: Figma Adds Google Drive and Internal Weave Tool Sharing (1 minute read)
item.description: Figma's agent and Make can now pull research, data, and images from Google Drive into a design conversation and create new Drive files. Connectors reach every plan, including Starter, though Google Drive is unavailable with the Governance+ add-on. Organization and Enterprise teams can also publish Weave tools internally, beside Figma's own and Community tools in the Tools tab.

item.title: Nubank unveils global brand refresh by Koto ahead of US launch (4 minute read)
item.description: Koto has refreshed Nubank's global identity ahead of its US expansion, creating a flexible brand system designed to accommodate more than 140 million customers and an expanding portfolio of financial products. The redesign retains the recognizable Nu logo while refining its signature purple, introducing proprietary Nu Sans Display and Nu Sans Text typefaces, and establishing a global library of photography, illustration, and motion assets. The system also extends into conversational AI, in-app animations built with Rive, and a redesigned global website, bringing greater consistency to Nubank's growing international presence.

item.title: Is this the most controversial font since Comic Sans? (3 minute read)
item.description: AI-generated posters are becoming recognizable through their repeated use of aggressive, upward-slanting brushstroke lettering, prompting comparisons with the much-maligned Comic Sans. ChatGPT attributes the repeated aesthetic to training data that associates oversized, distressed lettering with dramatic, attention-grabbing advertising and promotional graphics. Unlike Comic Sans, which was designed for a specific communication purpose, the AI-generated lettering often imitates expressive typography without understanding its context, turning a once-distinctive style into a visual cliché.

item.title: Design Feedback for AI Agents (3 minute read)
item.description: Design systems and agent instructions can guide AI-generated interfaces toward consistency, but they cannot anticipate every combination of components, layouts, and product states. A lightweight feedback loop helps close the remaining gap by letting designers annotate screenshots, comment in Figma, or provide spoken and written instructions that agents use to correct visual problems. Intent now integrates this workflow through a macOS screen-feedback feature, while human judgment remains essential for deciding which corrections should become reusable design system rules.

item.title: What does design system AI readiness mean, anyway? (12 minute read)
item.description: Making a design system AI-ready requires more than machine-readable documentation, design tokens, MCP servers, and agent skills. AI agents need constraints that guide them toward approved components, patterns, and implementation rules while reducing opportunities for inconsistent or invented solutions. The real measure of readiness is whether AI can participate in the design process without lowering quality, with human judgment remaining essential wherever tacit knowledge and context cannot be fully encoded.

item.title: “Designing a Good Poster is a Dark Art” – Highlights from This Year's INTL Poster Competition (8 minute read)
item.description: This year's INTL poster competition drew 2,670 entries from 78 countries, with 190 posters by more than 200 designers on display in Glasgow from November 12–22. Co-founder James Gilchrist calls a great poster near-impossible to design and singles out three trends: layered surfaces, 1990s-inspired collaged typography, and deliberately unprofessional, playful work.

item.title: Superior Type's Heaven is a sans serif built on oversized round shapes (3 minute read)
item.description: Superior Type's Heaven is a brutalist grotesque designed by Petr Kucera around oversized rounded shapes that appear compressed into rectangular spaces. The typeface includes four families, Heaven 01, 03, 06, and 09, each offering 18 styles from Thin to Black with italics, Latin and Cyrillic support, and a SuperVariable version that transitions from soft, rounded forms to boxier geometry. Distinctive curved letterforms, unconventional diagonals, and optional alternates give designers flexibility for expressive logos and display typography while retaining enough balance for longer text.

item.title: Designing a better future: your guide to design contribution in Open Source (12 minute read)
item.description: Open-source projects often lack the UX expertise needed to make powerful software approachable, while designers struggle to discover contribution opportunities in developer-oriented environments such as GitHub. Meaningful contributions can include user research, clearer project descriptions, onboarding improvements, navigation, error messages, accessibility, and better documentation of design processes rather than just visual assets. Designers can begin by exploring projects they already use, reviewing contribution guidelines, finding relevant issues, and collaborating directly with maintainers, even without extensive technical knowledge.

item.title: Canva Unveils Brush, an AI Model Built to Edit Designs at Lower Cost (5 minute read)
item.description: Brush, Canva's in-house vision-language model, edits designs up to 69% faster than the previous design agent at 46% lower cost per task. It reads both content and layout across full designs like multi-page decks, writes and runs small pieces of code, and inspects results before each next step. Brush is in beta for Canva Pro subscribers, with Brand Kit support and better image-heavy layout handling planned.

item.title: Amstel Updates Global Visual Identity to Highlight Amsterdam Heritage (2 minute read)
item.description: Amstel has redesigned its packaging and logo around its 1870 Amsterdam origins, adding bespoke typography inspired by historic canal bridge signage and a refined golden circle. The red, white, black, and gold system also features a wave pattern, a horizontal split evoking the Amstel River, and three coins representing the founders, city, and waterway. Already a Red Dot winner, the identity is rolling out across 11 markets, with all remaining territories due to transition by the end of 2027.

item.title: Design is more than creation (4 minute read)
item.description: Design is the deliberate process of deciding how something should work, respond, and be experienced, not simply the act of producing something that looks convincing. Conditions such as accessibility needs, localization, unpredictable content, failures, and different input methods should shape software from the beginning rather than being treated as edge cases to fix afterward. AI makes polished software dramatically faster to create, but that speed increases the importance of understanding which decisions were made, which assumptions they rely on, and whether they survive contact with reality.

item.title: How We're Training a Figma-Fluent Editing Model (4 minute read)
item.description: Specialized post-training lets Figma's first-party editing model compete with frontier models on precise, iterative edits to existing designs. A Llama 3.3 70B model trained on 250,000+ examples first became competitive with top models, but imitation learning limited generalization, so Figma now invests in reinforcement learning. Since beta, typical tasks run about 20% faster, users rate results 33% higher, and they undo the agent's work 60% less often.

item.title: Experience Design: Dropping the “User” from “User Experience” (6 minute read)
item.description: AI agents complicate the traditional definition of UX because people may increasingly accomplish goals without directly interacting with the companies, applications, and interfaces involved. Experience design provides a broader framing that includes traditional UX while also considering digital systems used by agents acting on humans' behalf and journeys involving multiple human and nonhuman actors. People's goals remain central, but designers must now consider experiences in which the immediate user of a product may be an AI rather than a person.

item.description: AI makes generating images and concepts easy, so the harder work is deciding what is worth making, whose perspective is missing, and whether it communicates. At DesignThinkers, RGD's annual conference in Toronto, speakers covered information design, blending strategy with creativity, and designing a city. AI-accelerated trends risk polished sameness, so "raw, messy curiosity is the most valuable thing we can bring to the table."

item.title: How to Write Better Copy for Graphic Design Projects (6 minute read)
item.description: Better graphic design copy starts with the project's purpose: a plain-language explanation, the audience, the most relevant benefit, objections, and the desired next step. Specific details persuade where vague praise does not, and a consistent brand voice should sound like the owner speaking face to face. Copy must fit its space, CTAs must match the reader's decision stage, and a final proofread should test every link and QR code.

item.title: Studio Kiln designs an identity for Reset that adapts like its app (4 minute read)
item.description: Studio Kiln's identity for Reset reflects the weight-loss app's personalized approach to eating, building flexibility and responsiveness directly into its visual system. A dynamic identity uses typography, color, imagery, and graphic elements that can shift across different contexts while maintaining a recognizable core. The result gives Reset a distinctive presence without locking a product built around personalized meal guidance into a rigid visual language.

item.title: The Window with No Buttons (9 minute read)
item.description: Style Dictionary, Storybook, and AI coding agents all run from the terminal, a blank window that feels like a wall to designers used to canvases.

item.description: François Bourdin, a French freelance concept artist, character designer, and illustrator in Nantes, creates dynamic characters from razor-sharp angular linework and vivid, saturated neon palettes.

item.title: WhatsApp group chats get permanent message pins, private Status updates, and more (3 minute read)
item.description: WhatsApp is adding four features designed to make busy group conversations easier to manage, including permanent message pins and Group Status updates visible only to members of a particular group. A new filter collects unread conversations containing mentions, direct replies, or @all messages so users can quickly find messages that need their attention. Recent message history can also now be shared with someone after they have joined a group, helping new members catch up without exposing older conversations automatically.

item.title: Meta Quietly Launches an AI Fashion App Called Style Sketch (2 minute read)
item.description: Meta's Style Sketch is an AI app that builds a virtual closet from a user's Instagram photos and suggests outfits from clothes they already own. Virtual try-ons use a model reflecting the user's body shape and skin tone, and trip plans pack outfits around destination, activities, and weather. The app launched on iOS and Android in Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand, with no word on a wider rollout.

item.title: The iPad is Finally Getting the Affinity App Creatives Have Been Asking For (2 minute read)
item.description: Affinity's all-in-one creative app is finally coming to iPad, nearly a year after its desktop debut, answering long-standing demands since new-format files can't open in the older V2 iPad apps. It combines photo editing, vector design, page layout, and sketching, with Apple Pencil support for pressure, tilt, and barrel roll, plus RAW editing and formats like PSD, AI, INDD, and SVG. The app is free for individuals despite its “pre-order” label, though Canva AI Studio features require a premium plan.

item.title: “This wasn't a thoughtfully designed menu.” (4 minute read)
item.description: Hawaii's 2018 false missile alert demonstrates how poor information architecture, ambiguous labels, and insufficient friction can turn an interface mistake into a real-world emergency affecting 1.4 million people. The alert system reportedly placed confusingly named test and real commands together without clear hierarchy or confirmation proportional to the consequences, making a catastrophic selection surprisingly easy. The same principles apply to everyday software on a smaller scale: visually similar choices, weak labeling, and poorly structured menus create countless small errors that gradually erode usability and trust.

item.title: There Will Always Be Someone Faster, Cheaper, and Better (8 minute read)
item.description: AI intensifies designers' fears about competing with people who can work faster, cheaper, or better, but those pressures have existed throughout the history of professional design and every major shift in production tools. Faster tools become threatening when designers price their time rather than outcomes, while “better” extends beyond the quality of an artifact to the experience, perspective, judgment, and relationships a designer brings to a client. As AI makes production faster, deliberately taking time to gain experience, make mistakes, and develop a singular way of working may become more valuable than racing to master whichever tool is currently dominant.

item.title: Design Systems Should Be Fast by Default (18 minute read)
item.description: Slow design system components make every app built on them slow, so performance belongs next to accessibility on the team's priority list. Timing ten popular systems on a 249-country dropdown and 100 checkboxes found Fluent and Carbon quickest to open the dropdown and Ionic by far the slowest. Playwright tests with explicit budgets, virtualized long lists, and published performance numbers keep components fast by default.

Dutch lighting consultancy Eclectic Lighting bridges that gap with sector-based project filters, a four-step process, specific client reviews, and a floor plan upload. Asking for a floor plan visitors already have turns the contact form into a concrete next step.

item.title: COPUS and Kontrapunkt design JUNO the bakery's cookie brand and site (4 minute read)
item.description: Kontrapunkt extended Copenhagen's JUNO the bakery into a restrained identity and packaging system built around white paper, subtle blue accents, simple duotone illustrations, and the bakery's blue peacock mascot. Its Danish Butter Cookies use the same quiet visual language. COPUS and Tommy Campbell carried the identity into JUNO's first online shop, using blue sparingly for highlights, product tiles, and the add-to-cart button to make the digital experience feel like a window into the physical bakery.

item.title: I Gave My Website a Boss Fight (11 minute read)
item.description: Missing the personality of the old internet, Paul Bakaus rebuilt his personal website over ten days with Claude Code as a retro Amiga-style world, using a 4,096-color palette, live-synthesized music, and a boss fight against a monster called Jirasaurus. Each page became a themed scene, from a rooftop panel and a speaking auditorium to a floppy-disk office platformer, and three pages hide playable games. Claude wrote the code, built the art pipeline, and composed the music, but animation needed a leg rig and constant feedback, and the site stays a fast, optional-to-play Ghost theme where reading still comes first.

item.title: This Horse-Shaped Headset Asks Designers to See the World Through Animal Eyes (6 minute read)
item.description: Equine Eyes, an oversized horse-head headset, uses side-mounted cameras and a VR display to simulate a horse's nearly 350-degree field of view and blue-yellow color perception.

item.title: This Artist is Using 90s Anime Aesthetics to Create the Ultimate Nostalgic Masterpieces That Will Hit You Right in the Feels (1 minute read)
item.description: Japanese-American illustrator Mike Yoshimura channels 80s and 90s anime, retro cyberpunk, and vintage cel animation into solitary figures in neon-lit rain and twilight cityscapes.

item.title: How this artist turned childhood nightmares into video game monsters (6 minute read)
item.description: John Kenn Mortensen translated his hand-drawn creatures and childhood fascination with darkness into the fantasy roguelike FLASK, combining grotesque medieval imagery, black humor, Labyrinth-like fantasy, and the energy of Slayer while working with a game art team to preserve his distinctive style in a colorful digital world.

item.title: Fitbit Edge: Premium Design for an Active Life (4 minute read)
item.description: Fitbit Edge pairs the brand's largest, brightest Hybrid OLED tracker display with a tactile side button for quick control mid-workout, even with sweaty fingers. A subtly curved chassis of 100% recycled aluminum keeps sensors against the wrist for 24/7 heart-rate and sleep tracking. Four finishes, four redesigned band styles, and up to seven days of battery life round out the design.

item.title: Windows Security is finally getting the Windows 11 makeover it should've had years ago (2 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft is redesigning Windows Security to finally align its interface with the rest of Windows 11, replacing layouts and visual elements that still feel inherited from an older generation of Windows. Navigation, typography, spacing, colors, controls, dialogs, and status indicators are being modernized, with layouts also adapting more consistently across different window sizes. The update additionally improves how security status and available actions are communicated, while device information on supported managed PCs will progressively load so useful details appear sooner.

item.title: OpenAI now lets you text your ChatGPT Dot agent to get things done (3 minute read)
item.description: ChatGPT Dot can now communicate through iMessage and RCS, letting users assign tasks, send photos or voice notes, and receive proactive updates without opening ChatGPT. Dot can use context from ChatGPT conversations and connected channels to decide where updates belong, while users can specify that only urgent information should arrive by text and approvals still happen inside ChatGPT. The beta is currently limited to ChatGPT Pro users in the US, with one-to-one messaging supported but no group chats, regular phone calls, or FaceTime.

item.title: The System I No Longer Know by Heart (6 minute read)
item.description: Working with AI agents means the author no longer memorizes every detail of the design system they build, a shift that requires making systems legible to LLMs. That knowledge has to move into the system itself, through explicit naming, current documentation, and composition rules, since agents can't rely on informal context or unwritten history. Understanding why the system works still matters, but less inventory in the designer's head is a trade worth taking if the system knows more about itself.

item.title: Building an AI-ready design system library: Code → Figma with MCP. Hands-on guide (15 minute read)
item.description: Figma captures only part of the behavior encoded in production components, leaving AI to invent missing details such as focus order, error states, accessibility behavior, and failure handling when translating designs directly into code. Reversing the workflow makes code the source of truth and Figma its visual mirror, with AI and MCP transferring real tokens, styles, properties, variants, and states from a repository into a usable design library. Storybook provides designers with a visual view of the production system, while explicit documentation of anything that cannot be represented in Figma helps maintain parity instead of allowing invisible differences to accumulate.

item.title: Nobody Asked for the Sparkle Button (13 minute read)
item.description: Products, from note apps to banks, ship the same AI chat panel behind a sparkle icon, often switched on by default and hard to turn off. Big cloud firms are projected to spend more than their cloud revenue on capex, while a cited study found that 95 percent of companies saw no measurable return from generative AI pilots. The fix is to build features with AI, not AI features, and to ask who asked, what it's named after, and whether it survives off by default.

item.title: Designing a skill (5 minute read)
item.description: Agent skills can be treated like apps whose interfaces happen to be written largely through instructions, with both the human invoking the skill and the AI interpreting it acting as users. Building a polished skill requires many familiar design practices, including finding the right form, refining copy, creating a visual system, anticipating repeated use, offering meaningful customization, and testing across different contexts. Precise instructions matter because agents fall back on familiar patterns when given vague directions, making skills a useful place to encode the context, trade-offs, intuition, and taste that individual prompts cannot reliably communicate.

item.title: You Are the Best Artist (1 minute read)
item.description: Art is less about conveying emotion to an audience than about capturing it, since a painter alone in a studio still makes art. Comparing skills with others can help, but becoming a better artist is personal, because nobody can express someone's feelings like they can.

item.title: This 3D Artist Achieves Incredible Realism to Breathe Life into Striking Character Designs (1 minute read)
item.description: A smug goblin, an albino demon, an adolescent chimp, and a dark elf showcase the striking realism of Australian 3D artist Tom Newbury.

item.title: Apple launches its new touchscreen MacBook Pro (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro comes in 14- and 16-inch sizes, pairing a PROLED XDR display with a Dynamic Island-style cutout and a lighter body. A redesigned hinge keeps the screen steady during touch input, while M5 Pro and M5 Max chips power both models. Prices start at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model, with preorders opening October 30 and availability beginning November 6.

item.title: Google Photos Rolls Out a Customizable Redesign of Your ‘Collections' Tab (3 minute read)
item.description: Google Photos on Android is getting a customizable Collections tab that lets users pin frequently opened collections, hide sections they rarely use, and rearrange the layout. Favorites, Screenshots, and Trash are pinned by default, while albums, people and pets, places, and other categories get carousels that can be hidden or reordered. The update arrives with Google Photos version 7.97 through a server-side switch, with no broader release date announced.

item.title: We're Announcing Genie 4, Our New World Model for Real-Time Interactive Simulation (1 minute read)
item.description: Google's Genie 4, a new world model for real-time interactive simulation, brings more realistic visuals and native audio to generated worlds. Natural-language prompts steer scenes live, from moving the camera to changing the weather or adding characters. Rollout starts with a limited group of trusted testers, with Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early-access Gemini API partners coming soon.

item.title: Designing for People with ADHD (9 minute read)
item.description: ADHD affects about 5% of people and stems from differences in how the brain develops focus, planning, and self-regulation. It is not a matter of willpower. Helpful patterns include reminders for unfinished drafts, chunked long forms, gradual disclosure of options, and visible progress, while autoplay and infinite scroll are best avoided. ADHD often overlaps with autism, dyslexia, and anxiety, so designing for it tends to help several groups at once.

item.title: One size doesn't fit all: rethinking “good design” across cultures (9 minute read)
item.description: Ideas such as clarity, simplicity, restraint, and functionality are often treated as universal measures of good design even though they emerged from particular Western histories and cultural contexts. Design traditions excluded from the dominant canon can use decoration, complexity, symbolism, and craft in ways that are deeply functional within their cultures, challenging assumptions that minimalism is inherently more sophisticated or understandable. Evaluating design more broadly requires asking who established prevailing standards of taste, whose histories were documented and taught, and whether a design successfully serves its specific cultural purpose rather than conforming to a supposedly universal aesthetic.

item.title: A select should tell you something (6 minute read)
item.description: Customizable HTML selects can now include previews, secondary information, warnings, and other context that helps people recognize the right option instead of deciphering text labels. Practical examples include showing fonts in their actual typefaces, displaying current local times instead of UTC offsets, aligning delivery prices for comparison, and distinguishing people with identical names by job title and department. The technique progressively enhances the native `select`, so unsupported browsers can retain familiar controls while richer desktop experiences provide more useful information without replacing built-in semantics and keyboard behavior.

item.title: Animated Architecture Diagrams from Plain Text (Website)
item.description: Declare semantic nodes, flows, and timed beats in reviewable text. Markdy compiles browser-native motion graphics that stay version-controlled, PR-friendly, and AI-native.

item.title: Open-Source CAD for AI Agents (Website)
item.description: The text-to-cad plugin gives your agent local workflows for generating 3D models as STEP, GLB, STL, or 3MF files. It also does design for manufacturing checks, generates engineering drawings, and connects to popular 3D printing, sheet metal, and CNC fabrication services.

item.title: Make Wild Visual Effects in Your Browser (Website)
item.description: Ladybug is an effects studio for pictures, video, type, and sound.

item.title: The Software Factory Forgot About Design (4 minute read)
item.description: A four-station workflow of Linear, Paper, a coding agent, and review brings design into the software factory, where issues otherwise turn straight into pull requests. Linear holds the intent, Paper hosts agent-drafted HTML and CSS designs made before implementation, and the coding agent builds from both issue and design. Review checks the build against intent, but agents still lack the history behind decisions, such as past designs, analytics, and design-system reasoning.

item.title: The New York Times turns 175 with an identity, events and a campaign (6 minute read)
item.description: The New York Times is marking its 175th anniversary with a visual identity, campaign, and program of events that use the publication's history as material rather than simply commemorating its age. Familiar elements from its editorial and typographic heritage are reframed across contemporary applications, connecting decades of journalism with the publication's current cultural role. The system demonstrates how an established institution can celebrate recognizable brand equity while giving historical assets new relevance instead of replacing them.

item.title: How Mother Design turned a séance into a new identity for Purple Garden (6 minute read)
item.description: Mother Design began Purple Garden's rebrand with a séance, chakra reading, and automatic drawing workshop, using the resulting forms and feelings to build an identity around spirituality as “A Living Practice.” A whimsical wordmark, crystal-like guidance glyph, warm purple palette, tactile imagery, living typography inspired by cymatic patterns, and expressive motion create an immersive system without relying on familiar psychic-industry clichés. The process moved between physical experimentation, traditional design software, and AI tools, deliberately introducing unpredictability into both the creative process and the finished identity.

item.title: This Creative Agency's Website is Giving Me Tumblr 2000s Vibes, and I'm Here for It (3 minute read)
item.description: Denver's Bound Agency has a handmade, scrapbook-style site by Wunder Werkz that evokes 2000s Tumblr, with a handwritten logo, doodled icons, and tarot cards.

item.title: struggle together (5 minute read)
item.description: AI can remove much of the difficulty involved in learning and making things, but some of that struggle builds judgment, understanding, relationships, and the ability to create things with other people that none could have made alone.

item.title: Stefan Sagmeister's Artworks Turn Global Data into Good News at La Gaîté Lyrique (4 minute read)
item.description: Stefan Sagmeister's solo show "Finally, Something Good" at La Gaîté Lyrique turns UN and World Bank data into artworks arguing that health, democracy, and equality have improved.

item.title: New report slams Microsoft for leveraging dark patterns to force people to use Edge (4 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft continues using dark patterns, including misleading banners, default-browser restrictions, and forced actions, to steer Windows users toward Edge. Users outside the European Economic Area encounter more interference when downloading, setting, and keeping an alternative default browser, demonstrating how regulatory requirements can directly affect interface design. Windows features such as Search and Widgets can also bypass a user's chosen default and open links in Edge, reinforcing concerns that Microsoft's design decisions undermine meaningful browser choice.

item.title: Franki Branding: Inside Koto's New Identity (3 minute read)
item.description: Koto's identity for restaurant discovery app Franki turns finding places to eat into the visual language of an insider's club, centered on bright yellow, oversized rounded typography, candid photography, and conversational copy. Diatype Rounded and a soft geometric symbol create a friendly foundation, while phrases such as “If we know, you know” reinforce Franki's positioning as a knowledgeable friend rather than a conventional recommendation platform. Motion extends through typography, UI, and content to suit the video-first product, while the same system carries into Franki Social Club and physical experiences.

item.title: Access Video and Image Models from Figma Weave via the Figma MCP (1 minute read)
item.description: Figma Weave's full lineup of video and image models, including Seedance, Kling, and Nano Banana, can now be used inside external AI agents through the Figma MCP. Users need a Figma Weave account connected to their Figma account to generate media mid-conversation. Each video or image generated with a Weave model consumes Weave credits.

item.title: 3 design principles in the AI age (5 minute read)
item.description: Three enduring principles remain essential to good design despite AI dramatically accelerating creative work: iteration, feedback, and connecting the dots. Faster generation makes exploring alternatives cheaper, but quality still requires repeated refinement, diverse human perspectives, and judgment about which feedback matters rather than accepting AI's first answer or treating it as the only critic. Designers also need time away from production to process accumulated knowledge and recognize larger connections, because AI can generate faster than humans can meaningfully reflect.

item.title: Design as a garden (2 minute read)
item.description: Creative work can be approached like tending a garden: cultivate favorable conditions, return consistently, encourage unexpected cross-pollination, and protect fragile ideas before judging them too quickly. Pruning unnecessary work and deliberately leaving room for play can be as important as producing more, while not every experiment needs an obvious payoff. Ideas also benefit from periods of inactivity and patience, making it useful to distinguish between moments that require greater effort and those that simply require more time.

item.title: Accessible Components Library (Website)
item.description: Accessible components with working examples, code, guidance, and the test scenarios to check them.

item.title: AI CAD Generator for Structured Parametric Models (Website)
item.description: Turn engineering intent into structured CAD with zCAD AI. Describe requirements, generate the model, inspect the result, and continue through revision.

item.title: Microsoft's identity for Copilot positions it as a tool for work (7 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft's evolving Copilot identity positions AI as a practical tool embedded in everyday work rather than an abstract futuristic technology. Its animated two-part mark, paired sans-serif and serif typography, gradients, and flexible graphic system create continuity across Microsoft's ecosystem while giving Copilot a recognizable presence of its own. The system is designed to scale across product interfaces, campaigns, and motion, balancing the expressiveness needed to represent generative AI with the clarity expected from a productivity tool.

item.title: Nine Checks Before Shipping a Product Email: A Workflow for Developers and Designers (7 minute read)
item.description: A product email can look right in a design file yet fail its reader through a vanishing action, a surviving staging link, or a duplicate send. Using a workspace invitation as the example, nine checks cover the message's behavioral contract, client compatibility, accessibility, captured application output, link validation, and retry handling. Delivery evidence, such as authentication and bounce handling, is reviewed separately after the template passes.

item.title: Estonian Street Artist is Transforming Ordinary City Walls into Bizarre, Cartoonish Masterpieces (1 minute read)
item.description: Estonian designer and street artist Ingmar Järve, known as Gutface, fills murals, prints, and digital work with distorted figures, deadpan faces, and satirical cartoon humor.

item.title: Apple exploring fix for Safari's cramped layout on the iPhone Duo's outer display (3 minute read)
item.description: Apple is exploring ways for websites to extend into the space behind Safari's right-aligned controls on the iPhone Duo's outer display, potentially giving web designers more usable width without obscuring important content.

item.title: How Do You Create a Design to Last for 1,000 Years? (2 minute read)
item.description: Nebbia's Interlude, a climbable stone portal on a cliff overlooking Lake Whakatipu, is the second completed work in Paererewā's plan for 1,000 works lasting 1,000 years.

item.title: Figma Adds Enterprise AI Credit Controls and Admin APIs (1 minute read)
item.description: Enterprise admins in Figma can now set default paid AI credit access per user, choosing a monthly limit, full access, or none across organizations or billing groups. The limits cover purchased credits only and reserve nothing, so shared pools can still run dry. New admin REST APIs for teams, folders, and files, plus a block on employees opening Starter or Professional plans with company emails, round out the update.

item.title: Apple unveils all-new iPad mini: OLED, thinner design, more (3 minute read)
item.description: Apple's biggest iPad mini update yet introduces a slightly larger 8.5-inch OLED display with 24% thinner bezels, up to 1,200 nits of peak brightness, and an optional nano-texture finish. The 5.4mm-thick design adds IP67 water and dust resistance, an A20 Pro chip, a landscape 12MP Center Stage camera, Acoustic Display audio, faster connectivity, and fast charging. Pre-orders begin October 28 ahead of a November 6 release, with pricing starting at $699 for 128GB.

item.title: These clever apps show off the iPhone Duo's potential (9 minute read)
item.description: Developers are creating playful apps built around the iPhone Duo's folding design. Deck-Man turns albums into virtual cassettes, letting users load a tape with the phone open and close it to listen, complete with mechanical playback sounds. TypeDraw uses the fold as a notebook cover, with customizable paper, drawing tools, and fonts based on the user's handwriting.

item.title: Entering Atomic Design from the screen (10 minute read)
item.description: Atomic Design does not have to begin with small reusable components and work upward, as product teams can instead start with complete screens and discover their underlying structure from user behavior. A scope-first approach identifies what users can do, determines which data or interface region each action affects, and assigns responsibility for that logic before defining components. This helps reveal relationships that a simple interface inventory misses, producing components and templates based on behavioral boundaries rather than visual proximity alone.

item.title: How to Put Your Design System to Work with the Figma Agent (5 minute read)
item.description: A connected design library gives the Figma agent approved components and tokens, while guidelines attached to it encode rules, exceptions, and which variant to pick. Examples on an Examples page or attached to a prompt show how pieces combine, and reusable skills like a /design-system-audit handle repeat processes. Recurring agent mistakes signal that guidelines, library, or examples need updating.

item.title: AI UI Design Prompts: Describe the Interface You Want (10 minute read)
item.description: AI coding tools produce more distinctive interfaces when prompts describe not only a broad visual style but also typography, layout, hierarchy, density, colors, borders, and how specific interface regions should relate to each other. Applying Swiss-inspired, editorial, developer-workbench, and neo-brutalist directions to the same test-results viewer demonstrates how identical functionality can produce radically different compositions while preserving content and behavior. Effective iteration comes from evaluating the rendered interface against the task, then giving concrete feedback about problems such as oversized headings, misplaced controls, or wasted space rather than relying on vague aesthetic instructions.

item.title: Sketch as fast as you think (Sponsor)
item.description: The idea arrives before the artboard does. Goodnotes is a note-taking app for people who think on a tablet. Draw with your stylus on a canvas with no edges, then type to find any of it later.Try Goodnotes for free.

item.title: Turn an Idea into Something You Can Hold (Website)
item.description: UseIt Studio is an AI design co-pilot: describe what you want, change it with a sentence, and get it ready to print, cut, and fold.

item.title: The Video Studio Where AI Agents Edit with You (Website)
item.description: Give each channel a workspace, teach your agent a style with skills, and put several agents to work at once — on maps, whiteboards, and 3D and motion graphics.

item.title: Logo.dev MCP Server (Website)
item.description: Connect Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, or any MCP client to Logo.dev, and let your agent look up brands, logos, and brandmarks.

item.title: Options are expensive. Not having them has a cost too (3 minute read)
item.description: Oxygen is adding a setting that lets KDE users choose between symbolic and colorful action icons, but supporting that seemingly simple preference requires redrawing hundreds of icons individually at multiple sizes. Different pixel dimensions require distinct proportions and levels of detail rather than straightforward scaling, turning one interface option into thousands of assets that must be designed, tested, and maintained. User choice carries a substantial hidden cost, but removing choice also has consequences when people have different visual preferences, habits, and accessibility needs.

item.title: Conran Design Group rebrands luxury accommodation provider Cheval (4 minute read)
item.description: Conran Design Group has repositioned luxury accommodation provider Cheval around “Generous by design,” shifting the brand from a product-led proposition toward experiences defined by space, time, and attention. A new elongated C containing two horses references Cheval's Knightsbridge origins, while Season typography, deep teal, bespoke property emblems, and flag-inspired signage replace more generic black, white, and gold luxury conventions. The flexible identity supports Cheval's expansion across serviced apartments and branded residences while giving individual properties room to express their distinct locations and character.

item.title: Masani Pizza's identity celebrates the family that owns it (5 minute read)
item.description: Saint-Urbain built Masani Pizza's identity around the personality and family behind the restaurant, giving the brand a warm, characterful presence rather than relying on familiar Italian restaurant conventions. Expressive typography, illustrations, photography, and playful graphic details create a visual language that feels personal and rooted in the people running the business. The resulting system turns family character and hospitality into the restaurant's primary point of distinction across packaging, signage, merchandise, and other touchpoints.

item.title: Teenage Engineering is a Masterclass in Product Design (2 minute read)
item.description: Teenage Engineering's music gear pairs aluminum bodies, clearly labeled controls, and purposeful color with a consistent visual language across hardware and software.

item.title: Talented Digital Illustrator Creates Breathtaking, Solitary Worlds That Will Make You Want to Pause and Get Lost in Quiet Reflection (1 minute read)
item.description: Nishanul Nishat paints lone figures in vast, dreamlike landscapes, using soft color palettes and rich lighting to build atmospheric, narrative-driven scenes of quiet solitude.
